    74: ## Authenticity and bootstrap trust
    75: 
    76: `release/eggpack/install.sh --version X.Y.Z` is a **lower-assurance convenience
    77: path**. It downloads and runs the exact-version installer from GitHub over
    78: HTTPS. It does not independently authenticate that bootstrap or its manifest.
    79: The wrapper prints this trust limitation before downloading. Its
    80: `--candidate --sha256 --size` mode checks file integrity against the supplied
    81: values; those values are trustworthy only after they have been compared
    82: against the release notes, and both travel over the same TLS channel, so this
    83: is integrity against corruption — not authenticity against a compromised
    84: publisher. The wrapper verifies no signatures because releases carry none.
    85: 
    86: No production key or signed release exists, by maintainer decision (see
    87: [release signing](release-signing.md)). There is therefore no
    88: independently distributed trust key and no signed high-assurance path;
    89: the strongest available procedure is the checksums-and-consistency
    90: verification below. Its anchor is the GitHub TLS delivery channel plus the
    91: published digests: it detects corruption and mix-ups, but a compromised
    92: publisher account would defeat it. Use it from a trusted Linux x86_64 or
    93: aarch64 machine:
    94: 
    95: ```sh
    96: set -eu
    97: VERSION='X.Y.Z'
    98: case "$VERSION" in ''|*[!0-9.]*|.*|*.|*..*) exit 2;; esac
    99: case "$VERSION" in *.*.*.*) exit 2;; esac
   100: VERSION_REST="${VERSION#*.}"
   101: VERSION_PATCH="${VERSION_REST#*.}"
   102: case "$VERSION" in 0[0-9]*.*|*\.0[0-9]*.*|*.*\.0[0-9]*) exit 2;; esac
   103: case "$VERSION_PATCH" in *.*) exit 2;; esac
   104: TAG="v$VERSION"
   105: BASE="https://github.com/dbowm91/wg-basic/releases/download/$TAG"
   106: WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
   107: chmod 700 "$WORK"
   108: STAGE=
   109: cleanup() { if [ -n "$STAGE" ]; then sudo rm -rf -- "$STAGE"; fi; rm -rf -- "$WORK"; }
   110: trap cleanup EXIT
   111: trap 'exit 1' HUP INT TERM
   112: curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' \
   113:   --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60 "$BASE/release-manifest.json" \
   114:   -o "$WORK/release-manifest.json"
   115: curl --fail --silent --show-error --location --proto '=https' --proto-redir '=https' \
   116:   --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 60 "$BASE/install.sh" -o "$WORK/install.sh"
   117: # No signatures exist to check. Compare the manifest digest bindings against
   118: # the digests published in the release notes before trusting the manifest.
   119: case "$(uname -m)" in x86_64) TARGET=x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu;; aarch64) TARGET=aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu;; *) exit 2;; esac
